title: Dispatch Built-ins
goal: Route recognized command names to built-in handlers instead of external execution.

narrative.hook: Your environment can successfully tokenize inputs and launch external system processes, but every single command is currently treated as an external binary lookup.
narrative.motivation: Executing internal state modifications through external processes is inefficient and fails to alter the persistent shell environment. Intercepting specific commands directly allows the shell to manage its own operations cleanly.
narrative.concrete_demo: When a user types a recognized control word, the shell intercepts it internally and performs the required action directly, bypassing external process creation entirely.

learning_objectives: Understand how to intercept specific command names before initiating external process lookups.
Design a routing mechanism to check input tokens against a set of internal command names.
Ensure unmatched commands correctly fall through to external process execution paths.
constraints: Must verify command names against registered built-in identifiers prior to any system execution calls.
Must preserve all existing input tokenization and parsing behavior from previous levels.
Must remain completely language-agnostic in all shared definitions.
deliverables: A command router module that intercepts known built-in names.
Integration of the router within the main execution loop to branch between internal handlers and external processes.

behaviors.description: Examine parsed command tokens and dispatch recognized identifiers to internal handlers instead of launching external processes.

tests.description: Verify normal routing of a recognized internal command.
tests.expected_behavior: The system intercepts the command and executes the internal handler.

tests.description: Verify fallback behavior for unrecognized command names.
tests.expected_behavior: Unrecognized commands bypass the router and attempt external process execution.

tests.description: Verify handling of empty or blank input lines during routing evaluation.
tests.expected_behavior: Empty input strings are safely ignored without triggering errors or false matches.

tests.description: Verify dynamic routing consistency across varied input sequences.
tests.expected_behavior: The command router correctly distinguishes internal commands from external binaries across randomized execution sequences.
